title: Seed acceptance given blocks with the canonical defaults

values: acceptance given section added or edited
facts.note: Diff-level observer must detect added/edited 'given' sections in acceptance criteria, regardless of author role, phase or file location.
Supporting signal only; does not gate activation. Any authoring of an acceptance given section is in scope.

fires: Anyone (planner, coder or tooling) authors a new acceptance criterion and writes its given section.
An existing acceptance given section is edited, e.g. auth, builders, time, stubbing or knobs are added, changed or removed.
An acceptance given section is written outside a formal planning phase or without a task that declares acceptance.
doesNotFire: Only the when/then parts of an acceptance are edited and its given section is untouched.
Documentation or wagon text is edited that contains no acceptance given section.

given: An acceptance criterion's given section is being authored or edited.
when: You fill in the given block (auth, builders, time, stubbing, knobs).
then: Start the given section from the canonical defaults: auth scopes [], builders [], time {}, stubbing policy strict with overrides [], knobs {}.
prefer: Add non-default values only where the acceptance's behaviour actually needs them.
Express any needed stub as an explicit entry in stubbing.overrides on top of the strict default.
When a harness template applies, let its given specialize these defaults instead of replacing them.
avoid: Granting auth scopes, adding builders, freezing time or setting knobs that the acceptance's behaviour does not require.
Relaxing the default strict stubbing policy merely to make an acceptance easier to satisfy.
why: A shared, minimal default given makes every criterion start from the same strict, permission-free baseline, so any extra setup is a deliberate, reviewable deviation.
evidence: Where a given field is not set by the acceptance, its effective value equals the canonical default (auth.scopes [], builders [], time {}, stubbing.policy strict, stubbing.overrides [], knobs {}).
Reviewer confirms each non-default given value is motivated by the acceptance's behaviour.
verifier_detail: Term given_defaults ('the default given block.') values: auth: {scopes: []}; builders: []; time: {}; stubbing: {policy: strict, overrides: []}; knobs: {}.
strict is the DEFAULT stubbing policy (applied when none is specified); this convention does not by itself reject an explicitly set non-default policy.

additions.text: Add non-default values only where needed; express stubs as explicit overrides; let harness templates specialize the defaults.
additions.justification: Operationalizes the defaults for the planner; the 'only what is needed' guidance is advisory, not part of then. Harness-template relation comes from graph.json edges.

additions.text: Adding unneeded auth/builders/time/knobs; relaxing the default strict stubbing merely for convenience.
additions.justification: Anti-pattern implied by the defaults being minimal and strict; advisory, does not turn the default into an invariant.

additions.text: Effective-value check for unset fields and reviewer confirmation of non-default values.
additions.justification: Source gives no verification method; this checks defaults as defaults without requiring explicit serialization of every field or forbidding non-default values.

additions.text: Rationale for a minimal, strict default baseline.
